<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|164|THE GOSPEL|CHA. IX.}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=9|verse=23}}† And he said to al, If any man vvil come after me, let him denie him self, and take vp his crosse daily, and folovv me. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=24}}† For he that vvil saue his life, shal lose it: for he that shal lose his life for my sake, shal saue it. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=25}}† for vvhat profit hath a man if he gaine the vvhole vvorld, and lose him self, and cast avvay him self? {{verse|chapter=9|verse=26}}† For he that shal be ashamed of me and of my vvordes, him the Sonne of man shal be ashamed of, vvhen he shal come in his maiestie, and his fathers, and of the holy Angels. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=27}}† And I say to you assuredly, There be some standing here that shal not tast death, {{sup|‖}} til they see the kingdom of God.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=28}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 17, 1. Mr. 9, 1.''}}* {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ The TRANSFIGVRATION.}}∷ And it came to passe after these vvordes almost eight daies, and he tooke Peter and Iames and Iohn, and vvent into a mountaine to pray. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=29}}† And vvhiles he prayed, the shape of his countenance vvas altered: and his raiment vvhite and glistering. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=30}}† And behold tvvo men talked vvith him. And they vvere Moyses and Elias, {{verse|chapter=9|verse=31}}† appearing in maiestie. And they told his decease that he should accomplish in Hierusalem. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=32}}† But Peter and they that vvere vvith him, vvere heauie vvith sleepe. And avvaking, they savv his maiestie, and the tvvo men that stoode vvith him. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=33}}† And it came to passe, vvhen they departed from him, Peter said to {{sc|Iesvs}}, Maister, it is good for vs to be here: and let vs make three tabernacles, one for thee, and one for Moyses, and one for Elias: not knovving vvhat he said. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=34}}† And as he spake these things, there came a cloud, and ouershadovved them: and they feared, vvhen they entered into the cloude. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=35}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''2. Pet. 1, 17.''}}* And a voice vvas made out of the cloude, saying, This is my beloued sonne, heare him. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=36}}† And vvhiles the voice vvas made, {{sc|Iesvs}} vvas found alone. And they held their peace, and told no man in those daies any of these things vvhich they had seen.

{{verse|chapter=9|verse=37}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 17, 14. Mar. 9, 17.''}}* And it came to passe the day folovving, vvhen they came dovvne from the mountaine, there mette him a great multitude. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=38}}† And behold a man of the multitude cried out, saying, Maister, I beseeche thee, looke vpon my sonne because he is mine only one. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=39}}† and loe, the spirit taketh him, and he sodenly crieth, and he dasheth him, and teareth him that he fometh, and vvith much a doe departeth renting him. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=40}}† And I desired thy disciples to cast him out, and they could not. {{verse|chapter=9|verse=41}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvering said, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Incredulitie hindereth the effect of Exorcismes, and other miraculous power giuen to the Church.}}∷ O faithles and peruerse<noinclude>{{rh|||generation,}}</noinclude>
